title: Pushes to main rebuild every image, not just the changed ones
description:
Each image in this repository has its own push-triggered workflow (`wgcw.yml`, `waml.yml`, `session-complete.yml`, `positron-sagemaker.yml`), and every one of them rebuilds unconditionally on any push to `main`. A change confined to `positron-sagemaker/` still spends runner time rebuilding WGCW, WAML, and Session Complete — the last of which is the largest build in the repo and runs on `ubuntu-latest-8x`.

The product image repositories don't have this problem. They call `posit-dev/images-shared/.github/workflows/bakery-build-native.yml`, which passes `--base-ref ${{ github.event.before }}` to `bakery ci matrix`. Bakery maps the push's changed files onto the image/version matrix and returns an empty matrix when nothing relevant was touched.

These workflows hand-roll their matrix job rather than calling the shared workflow — WGCW needs GCP workload identity federation, and Positron SageMaker needs the SOCI merge job — so they need the same change-awareness applied inline.

Scheduled weekly rebuilds and manual dispatches should continue to build the full matrix.

title: Configure pull-through cache for positron-sagemaker on public ECR
description:
The admin guide for Positron on SageMaker now documents a pull-through cache as an alternative to the manual docker pull/tag/push setup in Step 1. Configuring a pull-through cache in the platform-team account would allow the private `positron-sagemaker` ECR repository to be populated automatically from `public.ecr.aws/posit/positron-sagemaker` on first pull, removing the need for the weekly mirror workflow in platform-infra.

## What this involves

- Create a pull-through cache rule mapping a prefix (e.g. `ecr-public`) to `public.ecr.aws` in the platform-team AWS account
- Add `ecr:BatchImportUpstreamImage` to the SageMaker execution role so Studio Spaces can trigger upstream fetches
- Evaluate whether this replaces or complements the existing scheduled mirror workflow in platform-infra

title: Document a separate Positron space for SageMaker Unified Studio
description:
## Problem

In SageMaker Unified Studio, Positron does not start in the default space
of a project. The app fails with `InternalFailure`.

The cause is the AWS profile. Unified Studio runs a post-startup script on
every launch of the default space. This script writes `~/.aws/config` with
a `[default]` profile that has `credential_source` and no `role_arn`:

```
rm -f /home/sagemaker-user/.aws/config
aws configure set credential_source EcsContainer
```

The AWS CLI accepts this profile. The AWS SDK for Go does not. Our license
client (`license-manager-aws-sagemaker`) uses the Go SDK, so the license
checkout fails:

```
[license-manager] {"errorMessage":"credential type credential_source requires role_arn, profile default","level":"error","msg":"Unable to load SDK config"}
The license manager did not report an activated license. Positron requires a license to run in a hosted environment.
```

If the user has a `~/.aws/config`, `jupyter_server_config.py` does not
override `AWS_CONFIG_FILE`. In Unified Studio this file is always present.
As a result, Positron never uses the baked profile at
`/etc/positron/aws-config`.

## What works today

A user-created space works. Unified Studio does not run the post-startup
script in that space. No `~/.aws/config` exists, so Positron uses the baked
profile and gets a license.

We saw this pattern in 6 launches across 2 Unified Studio domains:

| Space | Post-startup script | Positron |
|---|---|---|
| default space | runs | does not start |
| user-created space | does not run | starts and gets a license |

Note: a user-created space does not have the `DomainExecutionRoleCreds`
profile. Unified Studio features that need this profile do not work there.

## Proposal

Document a separate Positron space. Do not change the default space.

Users keep the default space for Unified Studio work. Users open the
Positron space for Positron work. This split matches the limitation above.

Add these steps to the admin guide and the user guide:

1. Attach the Positron image to the Unified Studio domain.
2. Create a new space in the project.
3. Select the Positron image for this space.
4. Start the space.

Also remove the Studio Lifecycle Config approach from the docs. We tried a
lifecycle config to correct the profile. It never ran. A search of the
`/aws/sagemaker/studio` log group over 3 days returned no output from it.

## Out of scope

An image fix is possible, but it is a separate problem. `positron-server`
runs the binary named by `POSITRON_LICENSE_MANAGER_PATH`. A small wrapper
can pin `AWS_CONFIG_FILE` for that one process, so Positron and the
Unified Studio integration both work. Track this separately.

title: public.ecr.aws/posit/positron-sagemaker tags drifted: :latest/:2026.08.2-4 stale, only :2026.08.2 updated
description:
## Summary

`public.ecr.aws/posit/positron-sagemaker` tags have drifted from each other after the Sept 1 build (PR #74, commit `ff2e2a58`). Only the bare `:2026.08.2` tag was updated to the new build; `:latest`, `:2026.08.2-4`, and both `-ubuntu-24.04` variants are still pinned to the previous day's build (PR #75, commit `cca3f639`).

`ghcr.io/posit-dev/positron-sagemaker` is unaffected — all six alias tags there correctly point at the new build. The drift is isolated to `public.ecr.aws` (confirmed `public.ecr.aws/posit/...` and `public.ecr.aws/m0i8p2s7/...` are the same underlying repo/account, just two registry aliases — not two independent targets).

## Evidence

| Tag | Digest | Commit | State |
|---|---|---|---|
| `:2026.08.2` | `sha256:45c6fd57...` | `ff2e2a58` (Sept 1) | current |
| `:2026.08.2-4` | `sha256:50a243ca...` | `cca3f639` (Aug 31) | stale |
| `:latest` | `sha256:50a243ca...` | `cca3f639` | stale |
| `:2026.08.2-4-ubuntu-24.04` | `sha256:50a243ca...` | `cca3f639` | stale |
| `:2026.08.2-ubuntu-24.04` | `sha256:50a243ca...` | `cca3f639` | stale |
| `:ubuntu-24.04` | `sha256:50a243ca...` | `cca3f639` | stale |

`bakery.yaml` has exactly one `positron-sagemaker` version entry (`2026.08.2-4`), so a single build is meant to fan one image digest out to 12 tag refs (6 ghcr + 6 ECR Public). Only 1 of the 6 ECR Public writes actually stuck.

The Sept 1 run's `Merge/Push positron-sagemaker:2026.08.2-4` job log (run [33537518370](https://github.com/posit-dev/images-specialized/actions/runs/33537518370)) reports success and logs:

```
INFO  Verified ImageTarget(image='positron-sagemaker', version='2026.08.2-4', os='Ubuntu 24.04') ->
      ghcr.io/posit-dev/positron-sagemaker:2026.08.2, ...:2026.08.2-4, ...:2026.08.2-4-ubuntu-24.04,
      ...:2026.08.2-ubuntu-24.04, ...:latest, ...:ubuntu-24.04,
      public.ecr.aws/m0i8p2s7/positron-sagemaker:2026.08.2, ...:2026.08.2-4, ...:2026.08.2-4-ubuntu-24.04,
      ...:2026.08.2-ubuntu-24.04, ...:latest, ...:ubuntu-24.04
```

...i.e. it claims all 12 refs were verified, including the 5 public ECR tags that in fact never moved off the previous build. This is a false positive in `bakery ci publish`'s verify step, specific to `public.ecr.aws` (ghcr's 6 refs are all correctly verified and correct).

## Impact

Anyone pulling `positron-sagemaker:latest` (or `:2026.08.2-4`, or either `-ubuntu-24.04` tag) from public ECR gets a build that is a full day stale relative to `:2026.08.2`, silently.

## Ask

1. Re-run/patch the `merge` job (or manually re-tag) to push `latest`, `2026.08.2-4`, `2026.08.2-4-ubuntu-24.04`, and `2026.08.2-ubuntu-24.04` on `public.ecr.aws/posit/positron-sagemaker` to `sha256:45c6fd57...`, matching `:2026.08.2` and ghcr.
2. File/track upstream in `bakery` (images-shared): `bakery ci publish`'s post-push verification needs to read back *every* pushed tag ref individually on ECR Public rather than trusting a single success signal — it silently missed 5/6 tag writes here while reporting all verified.

title: Add composite action for syncing images to private ECR and SageMaker
description:
Implement a reusable composite action that mirrors a specific tag of `public.ecr.aws/posit/positron-sagemaker` to a private ECR repository and registers a SageMaker ImageVersion.

## Goals

- Mirror public ECR images to private registries for internal use
- Automatically register mirrored images as SageMaker ImageVersions
- Support scheduled runs without manual intervention
- Preserve full OCI artifact trees including SOCI indices

## Implementation details

The action will:
- Accept a tag, source image URI, and target ECR registry as inputs
- Skip ECR copy if the tag already exists in the private registry
- Skip SageMaker registration if the version is already registered
- Poll `describe-image-version` to verify successful registration
- Use ORAS to preserve OCI artifacts and SOCI index during copy
- Provide outputs indicating whether operations were skipped

See the action README for required IAM permissions and usage examples.

## Related

https://github.com/posit-dev/images-specialized/pull/77

title: Pin AWS_CONFIG_FILE for the license client so Positron starts in Unified Studio default spaces
description:
## Problem

Positron does not start in a SageMaker Unified Studio default space. The
app fails with `InternalFailure`. The license checkout is the cause:

```
[license-manager] {"errorMessage":"credential type credential_source requires role_arn, profile default","level":"error","msg":"Unable to load SDK config"}
The license manager did not report an activated license. Positron requires a license to run in a hosted environment.
```

## Cause

Unified Studio runs a post-startup script on every launch of a default
space. This script writes `~/.aws/config` with a `[default]` profile that
has `credential_source` and no `role_arn`:

```
rm -f /home/sagemaker-user/.aws/config
aws configure set credential_source EcsContainer
```

The AWS CLI accepts this profile. The AWS SDK for Go does not.
`license-manager-aws-sagemaker` uses the Go SDK, so it cannot load the
config.

Our image already carries a good profile at `/etc/positron/aws-config`.
`jupyter_server_config.py` (lines 594-611) does not apply it when a user
`~/.aws/config` exists. In Unified Studio this file always exists, so the
baked profile is never used.

## Proposed fix

`positron-server` runs the binary named by `POSITRON_LICENSE_MANAGER_PATH`.
Point that variable at a wrapper. The wrapper pins `AWS_CONFIG_FILE` for
that one process.

### 1. New file: `positron-sagemaker/<version>/license-manager-wrapper`

```sh
#!/bin/sh
# The AWS License Manager client uses the AWS SDK for Go v2. That SDK rejects a
# [default] profile that has credential_source and no role_arn. SageMaker
# Unified Studio writes such a profile to ~/.aws/config on every space launch.
#
# Pin this one process to the baked profile. positron-server, terminals,
# notebooks and the AWS Toolkit keep the AWS config of the user.
#
# AWS_PROFILE is cleared because the baked file defines only [default].
exec env -u AWS_PROFILE AWS_CONFIG_FILE=/etc/positron/aws-config \
  /usr/lib/positron-server/bin/license-manager-aws-sagemaker "$@"
```

### 2. Containerfile

Install the wrapper inside the existing
`if [ -n "${LICENSE_MANAGER_CLIENT_VERSION}" ]` block (lines 318-333). An
image built without the license client then stays the same. The `COPY` must
come before `USER $MAMBA_USER` (line 410).

```
COPY positron-sagemaker/<version>/license-manager-wrapper \
     /usr/lib/positron-server/bin/license-manager-wrapper
RUN chmod 0755 /usr/lib/positron-server/bin/license-manager-wrapper
```

### 3. `jupyter_server_config.py`

Add a wrapper path near line 532. Keep the test for the real client, so the
fallback does not change:

```python
 _LM_CLIENT_PATH = "/usr/lib/positron-server/bin/license-manager-aws-sagemaker"
+_LM_WRAPPER_PATH = "/usr/lib/positron-server/bin/license-manager-wrapper"
 _LM_CLIENT_PRESENT = _os.path.isfile(_LM_CLIENT_PATH) and _os.access(_LM_CLIENT_PATH, _os.X_OK)
+_LM_INVOKE_PATH = (
+    _LM_WRAPPER_PATH
+    if _os.path.isfile(_LM_WRAPPER_PATH) and _os.access(_LM_WRAPPER_PATH, _os.X_OK)
+    else _LM_CLIENT_PATH
+)
```

Then use it in `_lm_vars` near line 541:

```python
-        f"POSITRON_LICENSE_MANAGER_PATH={_LM_CLIENT_PATH}",
+        f"POSITRON_LICENSE_MANAGER_PATH={_LM_INVOKE_PATH}",
```

## Why the fix covers one process only

The stand-down logic at lines 594-611 is correct. Positron must defer to the
AWS config of the user for the IDE. This fix does not change that logic.

The baked profile runs its `credential_process` under
`env -u AWS_CONFIG_FILE -u AWS_PROFILE -u _AWS_CLI_PROFILE_CHAIN`. That
unset already prevents a profile cycle, so the wrapper is safe.

The wrapper also covers lease renewal and the lease return on `SIGTERM`.
Both go through the same entry point.

## Two alternatives we rejected

1. Add `AWS_CONFIG_FILE` to `_lm_vars` only. This is one line, but `_lm_vars`
   goes on the `/usr/bin/env` prefix of the `positron-server` command. Every
   child process inherits it, which includes terminals and R and Python
   sessions.
2. Set `AWS_CONFIG_FILE` in `AppImageConfig`. This needs no image change, but
   it applies to the whole container. `aws configure set` then targets
   `/etc/positron/aws-config`, which is owned by root and is read-only for
   `sagemaker-user`. The three Unified Studio profile writes fail, so
   `DomainExecutionRoleCreds` is never created.

## How to test

Start a default space in a Unified Studio project. The app log must show
both lines:

```
AWS: user config present at /home/sagemaker-user/.aws/config; not overriding AWS_CONFIG_FILE
Positron license acquired from the license manager (days left: ..., users: 50)
```

The first line does not change. That is correct. In the `PostStartup` log
stream, make sure that the script still creates `DomainExecutionRoleCreds`.

## Notes

`AWS_SDK_LOAD_CONFIG=1` is not needed. That variable belongs to v1 of the
AWS SDK for Go. The license client uses v2, which always reads the shared
config.

We saw this failure in 6 launches across 2 Unified Studio domains. A
user-created space is not affected, because Unified Studio does not run the
post-startup script there.

title: actionlint doesn't support GitHub's $/ self-repository uses: syntax
description:
zizmor's `self-repository` audit recommends replacing local action
references like `uses: ./.github/actions/sagemaker-mirror` with
GitHub's newer `uses: $/.github/actions/sagemaker-mirror` syntax.
actionlint v1.7.12 (latest release) doesn't parse `$/` yet and
reports it as an invalid ref format, which would fail this repo's
Lint check.

Revisit once upstream adds support, then apply `$/` syntax at the
locations below and drop any interim workaround.

- .github/workflows/positron-sagemaker-mirror.yml:79 (PR #88 branch, same file/line)

- https://github.com/rhysd/actionlint/issues/711

title: Add scheduled janitor workflow for public ECR image retention
description:
## Background

Amazon ECR Public has no lifecycle policies, so we need a scheduled janitor that enforces the retention policy settled in posit-dev/positron-sagemaker#18 on `public.ecr.aws/posit/positron-sagemaker` and `public.ecr.aws/posit/rstudio-sagemaker`:

- **Tagged images:** delete once `imagePushedAt` is 18+ months old. "Last updated" means last push, so a version that is no longer rebuilt ages out 18 months after its final build.
- **Untagged images:** delete once `imagePushedAt` is 30+ days old, **unless they are referenced by a kept image** (see below).
- **Protected floating tags:** never delete a digest tagged `latest`, `std`, or `min`.

Implementing this in Bakery (posit-dev/images-shared#745) was considered and dropped for now.

### ⚠️ Untagged ≠ unreferenced

`bakery ci publish` builds an OCI image index (`oras index-create`), and only the index carries tags. Its platform image manifest and SOCI index manifest are separate, **untagged** digests:

```
public.ecr.aws/posit/positron-sagemaker:latest   → OCI image index (tagged)
  ├─ sha256:2899…  image manifest      (untagged)
  └─ sha256:c8f2…  SOCI index manifest (untagged, artifactType application/vnd.amazon.soci.index.v2+json)
```

A naive "untagged and older than 30 days" rule would break pulls of every tagged image older than 30 days. The janitor must compute the set of digests reachable from kept tagged images and exclude it.

## Proposed design

### Script (`scripts/ecr-public-janitor`, Python stdlib, shelling out to `aws` + `oras`)

For each repository:

1. **Inventory:** `aws ecr-public describe-images --region us-east-1` gives you `imageDigest`, `imageTags`, `imagePushedAt` and the media type for each image.
2. **Tagged images to delete:** tagged images with `imagePushedAt` older than 548 days, excluding any digest carrying `latest`, `std`, or `min`. Refuse to proceed if the run would delete every tagged image in the repo.
3. **Keep set:** for every surviving tagged image, fetch its manifest anonymously (`oras manifest fetch …@<digest>`). Collect `manifests[].digest` and the `com.amazon.soci.*-digest` annotation values. Also keep any untagged manifest whose `subject` points into the keep set, which covers referrer-style artifacts.
4. **Untagged images to delete:** untagged, not in the keep set, and `imagePushedAt` older than 30 days. Children of tagged images deleted in step 2 fall out here in the same run.
5. **Delete:** `aws ecr-public batch-delete-image` (≤100 IDs per call), deleting indexes before the manifests they reference.
6. **`--dry-run`:** print the plan and delete nothing. Write a summary of what was (or would be) deleted to `$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY`.

Unit tests with fixtures covering: a tagged index with children (children kept), an orphaned child (deleted), an expired tagged image (deleted along with its children), protected floating tags (kept), and the "would empty the repo" guard.

### Workflow (`.github/workflows/ecr-public-janitor.yml`)

- Triggers:
  - weekly `schedule` in an open slot (e.g. `0 6 * * 1`)
  - `workflow_dispatch` with a `dry-run` input that defaults to `true`
- `environment: production`, using the `AWS_JANITOR_ROLE` secret from the companion platform-infra issue. `configure-aws-credentials` with `aws-region: us-east-1`, plus `oras-project/setup-oras`.
- Matrix over `positron-sagemaker` and `rstudio-sagemaker` with `fail-fast: false`.
- Slack notification on failure, matching the existing workflows.

## Rollout

- [ ] IAM role + `AWS_JANITOR_ROLE` secret in place (platform-infra issue)
- [ ] Merge the script and workflow with `workflow_dispatch` only
- [ ] Dry-run both repos. Confirm `describe-images` lists index children as untagged entries, and that no child of a current tag is in the delete plan
- [ ] Enable the schedule

title: Add Wiz scanning to SageMaker builds
description:
Production and development SageMaker builds need Wiz scanning without making image publishing depend on Wiz availability.

Add metadata generation and optional Wiz scanning to the SageMaker workflows so builds can be scanned when configured but still publish if Wiz setup fails.

title: Renovate never bumps the sagemaker-distribution base image (no repositories configured)
description:
The weekly `Renovate` workflow succeeds but does nothing. The latest run (2026-10-19) logs `WARN: No repositories found - did you want to run with flag --autodiscover?`.

`renovate.yml` sets neither `RENOVATE_REPOSITORIES` nor autodiscover, and the self-hosted `renovatebot/github-action` does not default to the current repo. As a result no bump PR has been opened since #70 added the custom manager.

Impact: `positron-sagemaker` still pins `sagemaker-distribution:4.4.1-cpu`; latest is `4.6.1-cpu`.

Fix: set `RENOVATE_REPOSITORIES: ${{ github.repository }}` in the workflow, and update the stale "no automated drift check" comments in the Containerfile and its template.

title: positron-sagemaker: upgrade OS and conda packages at build time
description:
## Background

During the eMudhra intermediate CA response (posit-dev/images-shared#849, #120) we found that `positron-sagemaker` **never upgrades existing OS packages**, so rebuilding it doesn't pick up security fixes like the patched `ca-certificates`:

- The base image is pinned: `FROM public.ecr.aws/sagemaker/sagemaker-distribution:4.4.1-cpu`. Renovate (`renovate.json`, regex manager on `-cpu` semver tags) bumps it when AWS publishes a new tag, but between releases the base's OS packages stay frozen at whatever AWS built.
- The template's only apt layer ("System packages") is `apt.install(...)`. It runs `apt-get update` + `apt-get install` for a fixed list of new packages but **no `apt-get upgrade`**. Packages already in the base (`ca-certificates`, `openssl`, `libssl3t64`, …) are never updated.
- Other images get OS updates through `apt.setup()` / `apt.run_setup()`, which call `apt.update_upgrade()` (`apt-get upgrade` + `dist-upgrade`). `positron-sagemaker` doesn't use them.
- The base ships a conda env (`/opt/conda`), and Python in that env typically uses conda's own `ca-certificates` / `certifi` bundle, not the OS one. An OS upgrade alone won't cover tools running in that env (Jupyter, `requests`, `pip`, …).

This image doesn't use a registry build cache, so cached layers aren't the problem. The template never asks for updates in the first place.

## Proposal

### 1. OS packages
Add a package upgrade early in the template, right after `FROM … / USER root` and before the "System packages" layer:

- Preferred: reuse the shared macro, e.g. `RUN {{ apt.update_upgrade() }}` (or fold it into the existing System packages `RUN` so there's still a single `apt-get update`, matching the template's "apt hygiene" comment block).
- Evaluate `dist-upgrade` carefully. The base is a curated AWS distribution, so check that a full upgrade doesn't break SageMaker components. If it does, fall back to `apt-get install --only-upgrade` for security-relevant packages (`ca-certificates`, `openssl`, `libssl*`, …), or plain `apt-get upgrade` without `dist-upgrade`.
- Update the template's header comments describing apt layer layout and load-bearing order.

### 2. conda env
- Check what the base's conda env uses for TLS trust: `conda list ca-certificates`, `python -c "import certifi; print(certifi.where())"`, `python -c "import ssl; print(ssl.get_default_verify_paths())"`.
- If it uses its own bundle, either update `ca-certificates`/`certifi` in the conda env (`micromamba`/`conda update`, as `$MAMBA_USER` or root, matching how the template already installs into the base env), or point it at the system bundle (e.g. `SSL_CERT_FILE` / `REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE` → `/etc/ssl/certs/ca-certificates.crt`). Document whichever is chosen.

### 3. Re-render and rebuild
- `bakery update files`, then rebuild via `positron-sagemaker.yml` (and the dev/preview variant workflow if it shares the template).
- Make sure the goss tests (`positron-sagemaker/test/goss.yaml.jinja2`) still pass. Consider adding a goss check that `ca-certificates` is installed at a minimum version, or that the curl test below fails.

## Verification

In the rebuilt image:
- `dpkg-query -W ca-certificates` shows the current Ubuntu 24.04 security version (`apt-cache policy ca-certificates` installed == candidate).
- `curl https://dv-g3b-emudhra.we-have-a-problem.com/` and `curl https://dv-g3b-aaa-emudhra.we-have-a-problem.com/` fail with a certificate error (exit 60) using the **system** curl.
- The same hosts fail from the **conda env's Python**: `python -c "import urllib.request as u; u.urlopen('https://dv-g3b-emudhra.we-have-a-problem.com/')"` raises `SSLCertVerificationError`.
- SageMaker Studio smoke test: the image still launches, and Positron and Jupyter work.

## Acceptance criteria

- Every rebuild of `positron-sagemaker` picks up current Ubuntu security updates for OS packages, not just when the base tag changes.
- The conda env's TLS trust store is current too, or is explicitly wired to the system store.
- The eMudhra test hosts are distrusted by both system tools and conda-env Python.

## Related

- #120: eMudhra rebuild for this repo (this image can't be fixed by a rebuild alone)
- posit-dev/images-shared#849: epic

title: Remove the non-functional registry cache from WGCW builds (treat like WAML)
description:
## Background

`wgcw.yml` was given a registry build cache in `dd44c8d` ("Cache WGCW builds in Artifact Registry", 2026-05-14). It points at `us-central1-docker.pkg.dev/cloud-workstations-cache` because the Workbench image is larger than GHCR's per-image size limit. **This cache has never worked:**

- **Reads always fail.** Every run's `--load` step tries to import the cache and gets a permission error. BuildKit treats this as a warning and builds without the cache. This happened in every run checked (push 39467087273 on Oct 20, scheduled 39097182767 on Oct 18 and 38111942128 on Oct 11), for both the minimal and standard variants:
  ```
  importing cache manifest from us-central1-docker.pkg.dev/cloud-workstations-cache/workbench-for-google-cloud-workstations/cache:2026.09.0-ubuntu-24.04-std-amd64
  ERROR: failed to configure registry cache importer: failed to authorize: ... denied:
  Permission "artifactregistry.repositories.downloadArtifacts" denied on resource
  "projects/cloud-workstations-cache/.../workbench-for-google-cloud-workstations" (or it may not exist)
  ```
- **Nothing ever writes to it.** bakery only adds `cache-to` when a build both pushes and has `--cache-registry`. The `--push` step doesn't pass `--cache-registry`, so even with working credentials the cache would never be filled.
- The `CACHED` steps in wgcw logs come from the `--push` step reusing layers the `--load` step built moments earlier on the same runner. They don't come from the registry.

So every WGCW build already runs from scratch on a fresh GitHub-hosted runner, the same as WAML, which has no registry cache. The cache setup only adds an import attempt per build, an `ERROR` line in the logs, and a misleading impression that WGCW is cached. (That impression led to #121 adding a `refresh-cache` input here during the eMudhra response, posit-dev/images-shared#849.)

## Decision

Treat WGCW like WAML: **no registry cache, because the image is too large to cache.** The broken Artifact Registry setup is just the leftover from an attempt to work around that limit. It isn't the reason for removing it.

## Tasks

- [ ] `wgcw.yml`: remove `CACHE_REGISTRY` and `--cache-registry` from the `--load` build step, so the command matches `waml.yml`.
- [ ] `wgcw.yml`: remove the `refresh-cache` workflow_dispatch input, the `REFRESH_CACHE` env var, the `CACHE_FLAGS` / `--no-cache` logic, and the "reads the registry cache but never writes it" comment added by #121. With no registry cache they do nothing: a fresh runner always rebuilds every layer.
- [ ] Add a short comment where the cache flags used to be, stating that WGCW (like WAML) is deliberately uncached because of image size, and that GitHub-hosted runners start without a local cache, so every build is a clean rebuild.
- [ ] Optional / infra: since image size rules out caching, decide whether to delete the unused Artifact Registry repository `projects/cloud-workstations-cache/locations/us-central1/repositories/workbench-for-google-cloud-workstations` (if it exists) and its retention rules. Coordinate with whoever owns the `cloud-workstations-cache` GCP project.
- [ ] Check docs/AGENTS.md for any mention of WGCW caching and update it. None was found in a quick grep.

## Acceptance criteria

- No `importing cache manifest` or `cache importer` errors in WGCW build logs.
- WGCW and WAML handle caching the same way (no `--cache-registry`, no `refresh-cache` input).
- Scheduled/push/dispatch builds otherwise behave as before.

## Related

- #120 and #121: the eMudhra rebuild for this repo, and the `refresh-cache` input this issue removes.
- posit-dev/images-shared#852 (monthly cache refresh): WGCW is out of scope there because it has no cache.

title: Rebuild production images for eMudhra CA compromise
description:
## Background

Part of the eMudhra intermediate CA compromise response (posit-dev/images-shared#849): https://emudhra.we-have-a-problem.com/. Eight eMudhra intermediate CAs (and their Sectigo cross-signs) had their private keys compromised. Clients that don't check revocation need an updated trust store (`ca-certificates`) so they stop trusting these intermediates.

These workflows call `bakery build` directly rather than the shared workflow, and each image gets its trust store in a different way. Each one needs its own plan:

| Image | Workflow | Where `ca-certificates` comes from | Registry cache | What's needed |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| workbench-for-microsoft-azure-ml | `waml.yml` | `ubuntu:24.04` + `apt.run_setup()` (runs `apt-get upgrade`) | none | Plain dispatch. GitHub-hosted runners start fresh, so the upgrade runs |
| workbench-for-google-cloud-workstations | `wgcw.yml` | GCW `base:public-image-current` + `apt.setup()` (runs `apt-get upgrade`) | **read-only** on the `--load` step | Dispatch with `--no-cache` (see posit-dev/images-shared#847) |
| rstudio-sagemaker | `rstudio-sagemaker.yml` | inherited from `ghcr.io/posit-dev/workbench-session:ubuntu-26.04-*`; no upgrade of its own | none | Rebuild **after** posit-dev/images-workbench#221 republishes `workbench-session` |
| positron-sagemaker | `positron-sagemaker.yml` | pinned `public.ecr.aws/sagemaker/sagemaker-distribution:4.4.1-cpu`; **no apt upgrade** | none | **A rebuild alone won't fix this.** Needs a template change (see below) |

## Tasks

- [ ] Confirm the relevant distros have shipped a `ca-certificates` update that distrusts the compromised intermediates
- [ ] `waml.yml`: dispatch on `main`
- [ ] `wgcw.yml`: once the `--no-cache` dispatch input from posit-dev/images-shared#847 lands, dispatch on `main` with it enabled. Also find out what (if anything) writes the `us-central1-docker.pkg.dev/cloud-workstations-cache` registry cache. This workflow reads it but never writes it, so stale layers will come back on later builds unless something refreshes it.
- [ ] `rstudio-sagemaker.yml`: after posit-dev/images-workbench#221 has republished `workbench-session` (`session.yml`), dispatch on `main`. `--pull` picks up the new base.
- [ ] `positron-sagemaker.yml`:
  - [ ] Add an `apt-get update && apt-get install --only-upgrade ca-certificates` (or the full `apt.update_upgrade()`) step to the template, or move to a patched `sagemaker-distribution` release if AWS publishes one
  - [ ] The base ships a conda env. Check conda's `ca-certificates`/`certifi` packages there too, since Python in that env may use its own bundle instead of the OS store
  - [ ] Re-render (`bakery update files`), merge, then dispatch on `main`
- [ ] Verify one rebuilt image per workflow:
  - `ca-certificates` version matches the patched release
  - `curl https://dv-g3b-emudhra.we-have-a-problem.com/` and `curl https://dv-g3b-aaa-emudhra.we-have-a-problem.com/` fail with a certificate error
- [ ] Confirm the new tags/digests were published to every registry each workflow pushes to (ECR mirror, GCP Artifact Registry, etc.)
